"""Update a GitHub pull request description with a CI status badge and a recap of the CI results.

This is the successor of the ``pr-ci-post-dashboard-link`` workflow which used to post (and delete) a
standalone comment on every run. Instead of leaving a trail of comments, this script edits the PR body
*in place*: it keeps a small status badge near the top and a detailed recap near the bottom, each wrapped
in dedicated HTML-comment markers so that subsequent runs simply replace the previous content.

The recap numbers are pulled from the pytest-observability Prometheus/Grafana stack. When those metrics
are not available (for instance the very first run, or a run that never produced test data), the recap
falls back to the information carried by the GitHub Actions workflow run itself. Runs where the code
quality job failed are highlighted, since in that case all the test jobs are skipped.

Example:

    python utils/update_pr_ci_dashboard_recap.py \\
        --sha "$HEAD_SHA" --run-id "$RUN_ID" --run-url "$RUN_URL" --run-conclusion "$RUN_CONCLUSION"
"""

import os


try:
    import requests
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - requests is always available in CI
    requests = None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Markers delimiting the sections we manage inside the PR body. They are HTML comments so they stay
# invisible when the markdown is rendered, while remaining easy to locate for an in-place update.
BADGE_START = "<!-- CI_DASHBOARD_BADGE_START -->"
BADGE_END = "<!-- CI_DASHBOARD_BADGE_END -->"
RECAP_START = "<!-- CI_DASHBOARD_RECAP_START -->"
RECAP_END = "<!-- CI_DASHBOARD_RECAP_END -->"

# Static shields.io badge used as a clickable link to the Grafana dashboard.
BADGE_URL = "https://img.shields.io/badge/CI%20Dashboard-View%20in%20Grafana-blue"

# Substrings identifying the *old* standalone dashboard comments (posted by the previous workflow).
# Any PR comment containing one of these is deleted so we don't keep stale duplicates around.
OLD_DASHBOARD_COMMENT_MARKERS = [
    "**CI Observability Dashboard:** [View test results in Grafana]",
    "**CI Dashboard:** [View test results in Grafana]",
]

# Base URL of the Grafana instance hosting the pytest-observability dashboards.
GRAFANA_BASE_URL = "https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool"

# Prometheus query endpoint. Overridable through the environment so the script can be pointed at a
# different datasource without touching the code.
PROMETHEUS_URL = os.environ.get(
    "PROMETHEUS_URL", f"{GRAFANA_BASE_URL}/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/v1/query"
)

GITHUB_API_URL = "https://api.github.com"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prometheus helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def prometheus_string(value) -> str:
    """Convert ``value`` to an escaped Prometheus string literal (double quoted).

    The returned value is ready to be dropped inside a label matcher, e.g.
    ``f"metric{{pr={prometheus_string(pr)}}}"`` produces ``metric{pr="123"}``.
    """
    text = str(value)
    text = text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n")
    return f'"{text}"'


def first_value(results) -> "float | None":
    """Extract the first numeric sample value from a Prometheus query ``result`` list.

    A Prometheus instant query returns entries shaped like ``{"metric": {...}, "value": [ts, "42"]}``.
    Returns ``None`` when there is no usable value.
    """
    if not results:
        return None
    try:
        return float(results[0]["value"][1])
    except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _prometheus_query(query) -> list:
    """Run an instant Prometheus query and return its ``data.result`` list (empty on any error)."""
    if requests is None:
        return []
    try:
        response = requests.get(PROMETHEUS_URL, params={"query": query}, timeout=30)
        response.raise_for_status()
        payload = response.json()
    except (requests.RequestException, ValueError):
        return []
    return payload.get("data", {}).get("result", [])


def get_metric_value(query, fallback_query=None, fallback_on_zero=False) -> "float | None":
    """Return the first value of ``query``, optionally falling back to ``fallback_query``.

    The fallback query is used when the primary query yields no value, and additionally when the
    primary value is exactly ``0`` and ``fallback_on_zero`` is set.
    """
    value = first_value(_prometheus_query(query))
    needs_fallback = value is None or (fallback_on_zero and value == 0)
    if needs_fallback and fallback_query is not None:
        fallback_value = first_value(_prometheus_query(fallback_query))
        if fallback_value is not None:
            return fallback_value
    return value


def get_latest_run_id(pr_number) -> "str | None":
    """Return the ``run_id`` label of the most recent pytest-observability series for a PR."""
    query = f"pytest_run_created{{pr={prometheus_string(pr_number)}}}"
    results = _prometheus_query(query)

    latest_run_id = None
    latest_timestamp = None
    for series in results:
        run_id = series.get("metric", {}).get("run_id")
        if not run_id:
            continue
        try:
            timestamp = float(series.get("value", [None])[0])
        except (TypeError, ValueError, IndexError):
            timestamp = None
        if latest_timestamp is None or (timestamp is not None and timestamp > latest_timestamp):
            latest_timestamp = timestamp
            latest_run_id = run_id
    return latest_run_id


def get_ci_recap(pr_number, run_url, run_conclusion) -> dict:
    """Collect the CI metrics for a PR into a dictionary consumed by :func:`render_ci_recap`."""
    run_id = get_latest_run_id(pr_number)

    selector = f"pr={prometheus_string(pr_number)}"
    if run_id is not None:
        selector = f"{selector}, run_id={prometheus_string(run_id)}"

    def metric(name, **kwargs):
        return get_metric_value(f"{name}{{{selector}}}", **kwargs)

    return {
        "run_id": run_id,
        "run_url": run_url,
        "conclusion": run_conclusion,
        "total": metric("pytest_tests_total"),
        "passed": metric("pytest_tests_passed_total"),
        "failed": metric("pytest_tests_failed_total"),
        "skipped": metric("pytest_tests_skipped_total"),
        "errors": metric("pytest_tests_error_total"),
        "duration": metric("pytest_duration_seconds"),
    }
